data.name: Radhakrishna
data.gender_notes: Radhakrishna is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: God in the form of Krishna
data.long_meaning: The combination of the names Radha (meaning 'pleasing to the senses') and Krishna (meaning 'all-attractive') represents the ultimate form of God who is the source of all pleasure and attractiveness. The name Radhakrishna carries the meaning “God in the form of Krishna” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Radhakrishna usually hope their child will grow to embody god in the form of krishna and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Radhakrishna is a divine name that represents the ultimate form of God who is the source of all love, pleasure, and attraction. It is a name that embodies the divine couple Radha and Krishna, who are the embodiment of love and devotion.
data.etymology: Radhakrishna belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God in the form of Krishna.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Radhakrishna total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: Radhakrishna is a revered name in Hinduism, particularly in the traditions of Vaishnavism and of the Bengali-speaking regions in India and Bangladesh. Krishna, as one of the most popular deities in Hinduism, is known for his playful, affectionate, and mischievous nature, making him a beloved figure across generations. Radha, on the other hand, is viewed as the eternal consort of Krishna, embodying the feminine aspect of the divine. Together, they represent the romantic and divine love story depicted in various Hindu texts like the Mahabharata and the Bhagavad Purana.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Radhakrishna refers to the absolute reality of the universe, representing the Divine Couple in their ultimate form. The spiritual significance of this name comes from the intensely passionate and devoted love between Radha and Krishna. Radha, in her unwavering love for her lord Krishna, embodies the highest spiritual ideal of devotion (Bhakti) and self-surrender. Similarly, Krishna, as the all-knowing, all-encompassing deity, represents the ultimate truth and wisdom (Jnanam).
data.spiritual_symbolism: Radhakrishna symbolizes the divine union of Radha (embodiment of love and devotion) and Krishna (god of love, compassion, and wisdom). This name represents the ultimate transcendence of earthly desires through the transformative power of love and devotion.
